Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-07
Time: 08:43 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (CSM), Avery Chen (SE), Noah Patel (Onboarding Eng), Mateo Ruiz (HorizonLedger Platform Eng), Lila Ng (HorizonLedger InfoSec), Sana Kapoor (ML/Prod Lead), Tom Brewer (DevOps)

Summary (auto):
Redwood and HorizonLedger reviewed pilot scope, success criteria, network/topology for a private VPC pilot, SSO/KMS requirements, and SLA expectations. Agreed next steps around runbook, sample dataset, security docs, and scheduling a load test week-of 2025-11-17.

Topics:
- Pilot scope & success metrics
- Private VPC networking & peering options
- KMS/HSM and encryption at rest
- RBAC/SSO integration and audit logs
- Observability and token-level billing in Redwood Console

Action items (brief):
See metadata.action_items list above for owners/dates.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Jordan Miles: alright good morning everyone, thanks for hopping on, I think we have about 45 minutes, we wanted to run through the pilot handoff and the SLA/questions from your security team, um Priya and Avery will cover the runbook items, and Noah will call out the staging steps.
[00:22] Mateo Ruiz: Hi, yeah thanks Jordan, quick context — we are trying to validate inference cost at scale and also test private deployment inside our AWS VPC, we want to confirm both latency SLOs and that logs/audit are available.
[00:37] Priya Shah: Great, that's the main success criteria we noted: latency under 120ms p50 for our 512-token baseline, throughput to sustain 100 concurrent sessions, and no PII persistence beyond TTL — is that still accurate?
[00:50] Sana Kapoor: Yes, 120ms p50 is our target for prod, pilot can be a little looser but we want to see trend and variance. Also we'll run model A and model B variants to compare cost/perf.
[01:05] Avery Chen: Quick note on models — Redwood can route requests to a quantized variant that lowers cost, but we need to map expected token distribution, that informs kernel selection and batching. If you send the sample prompts we can pre-profile.
[01:22] Tom Brewer: On networking, we prefer VPC peering over public egress; can we get a guide for firewall rules and the necessary CIDRs? Also curious about NAT, we have constrained egress.
[01:36] Noah Patel: Yes, we have a staging checklist for VPC mode — inbound/outbound ports, peering setup, security group templates. Avery will attach that runbook. For NAT we recommend an egress-only NAT for control-plane calls, but data plane stays within peered private network.
[01:55] Lila Ng: From InfoSec, two asks: 1) How do you handle KMS integration for model cache and logs? 2) Do you provide immutable audit logs and retention controls?
[02:08] Jordan Miles: Good questions. For KMS we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and can also integrate HSM — the pilot will exercise KMS for tokenized secrets. Audit logs are shipped to your logging destination and retention is configurable; we'll share the retention matrix but short answer: yes, immutable append-only logs are supported with export hooks.
[02:29] Lila Ng: Okay please send the SOC2/ISO artifacts and the KMS integration guide; also we need to see TLS cert rotation cadence.
[02:40] Priya Shah: We'll compile a security packet — SOC2 attestation, ISO summary, KMS + HSM docs, and cert rotation notes. Expect that by Tuesday but will aim earlier.
[02:51] Mateo Ruiz: A couple of gotchas from our side — our customer data contains nested JSON payloads up to 4k tokens, and we have a multi-tenant routing layer. Need to confirm per-tenant isolation and KV cache safety.
[03:06] Avery Chen: For KV cache we can scope cache keys per-tenant ID, and we have options to disable prefix caching if you want strict isolation. We'll call out the config in the runbook. Also for 4k tokens you may want to adjust kernel selection; we'll recommend a batch/seq configuration.
[03:28] Sana Kapoor: Regarding metrics, can Redwood surface per-route token cost and per-request latency in the Console? We want to feed that into our cost allocation.
[03:39] Noah Patel: Yes, Console has token-level billing breakdown and you can tag routes; we'll demo the cost views during the pilot onboarding session.
[03:50] Tom Brewer: About SLA — HorizonLedger requires a 99.9% uptime target and a 15 minute incident initial response for P1s. How does Redwood's Dedicated / Private offerings map to that?
[04:05] Jordan Miles: For Private deployments we offer an enterprise SLA that meets 99.9% with dedicated capacity options; for pilot we'll run in a sandboxed private deployment with operational support, but production SLA will be part of the Dedicated contract. We'll get legal to follow up with the SLA matrix.
[04:21] Lila Ng: Can we run a short replay test to validate log immutability and audit trails? We might need a preserved subset of logs for 30 days in an S3 bucket.
[04:33] Avery Chen: Absolutely — part of the pilot we'll configure export to your S3 and run a replay. We'll also set up a retention policy you can validate.
[04:44] Mateo Ruiz: Onboarding timeline — we want the pilot to start mid-November and run for three weeks with a load test in week one. What's realistic?
[04:55] Priya Shah: If we get the dataset and VPC details by 11/12, we can provision staging and do an initial smoke test 11/14, run the load test the week of 11/17 and then iterate. That's consistent with our internal plug schedule.
[05:12] Jordan Miles: Okay next steps recap quickly — Avery sends runbook and staging checklist, Mateo uploads sample dataset and Tom shares CIDR and peering contact, Lila to send security contacts and questionnaire. We'll schedule the load test slots and send calendar invites.
[05:30] Sana Kapoor: One quick tech question — how much does Redwood instrument for per-token KV cache hit rates? We want to compute cost savings threshold for enabling prefix caching.
[05:42] Avery Chen: Console reports cache hit rate metrics; we can also stream metrics to your Prometheus endpoint if you prefer. We'll include examples in the runbook on how to interpret those.
[05:56] Tom Brewer: Slight nit — some of our infra folks mentioned CloudX Endpoints offering simpler managed egress; curious how Redwood's private model compares on operational overhead.
[06:09] Jordan Miles: Totally fair — CloudX can be simpler but lacks the inference-optimized runtime we provide; part of pilot is to quantify operational burden and unit cost difference. We'll capture operational tasks in the runbook so you can compare.
[06:25] Lila Ng: Also we'd like to do a quick compliance call with your security lead later this month, maybe week of 11/10.
[06:33] Jordan Miles: I'll loop in our security lead and propose two slots for 11/11 and 11/12.
[06:40] Mateo Ruiz: Cool — any docs links now?
[06:43] Avery Chen: I'll drop the runbook link and the VPC template in the follow-up email, plus the KMS guide and SOC2 pack.
[06:51] Jordan Miles: Great — thanks everyone. We'll send the follow-ups and action items; Priya will own the pilot cadence.
[07:00] Priya Shah: Thanks all — we'll touch base after the load test prep.
[07:05] Meeting end.
